instruction: In the Tetris game settings, change the game speed to 30 FPS and the block size to 25 pixels.

command: import pyautogui; pyautogui.hotkey('ctrl', 's'); import time; time.sleep(0.5)

metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent opened VS Code with Tetris project, read through code files (main.py, tetris.py, block.py, settings.py), installed pygame, ran the game, but failed to identify and fix the rotation boundary check bug within 50 turns.
metadata.capability_extraction: Can open and navigate files in VS Code, use terminal to run commands, install Python packages, read and edit code files, use find/replace in VS Code
metadata.failure_analysis: Model could not identify the missing intersection check after rotation in tetris.py. Spent excessive turns reading code and re-running without applying the correct fix.
metadata.task_rationale: Simplified from bug-fixing to a straightforward config value change in settings.py, testing the model's ability to locate and modify specific constants.
metadata.explanation: Task requires changing GAME_SPEED from 60 to 30 and BLOCK_SIZE from 20 to 25 in settings.py. Getter reads settings.py via regex to extract both values. Metric awards 0.5 per correct value for partial credit.

llm_judge_reasons: Getter correctly reads settings.py and extracts GAME_SPEED and BLOCK_SIZE via regex, returning integer values
Metric correctly handles expected parameter as the rules dict directly (no incorrect nesting), checking expected_speed and expected_blocksize
Both instruction requirements (speed=30, blocksize=25) are fully covered with appropriate 0.5 partial credit each
Postconfig properly activates VS Code and sends Ctrl+S to ensure file is saved before getter reads it
Expected values (30 and 25) semantically match the instruction requirements
